## Summary

**STOREM** (Store masked register into memory): Store 8 byte from register-b in memory when its mask=1.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `b → <vea> depending on mask.` |
| Syntax | `STOREM b,mask,<vea>`<br>Where the lower 8 bits of d is used as mask to write (1) or not (0) |
| Short | Store 8 byte from register-b in memory when its mask=1 |
| Description | Store is a conditional write of 8 bytes. The selection is made by the last 8 bit of register d. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–8 | d (mask) |
| 2 | 7–0 | `00000101` |

- Not allowed &lt;vea&gt; : #imm
- No masking is done when destination is a register.
- Storeilm is similar

### Example

```asm
   storeilm    e10,e11,(a2)
```

```text
b e10: 11 22 33 44 55 66 77 88
d e11: .. .. .. .. .. .. .. 7C   ( $7c = binair %0111 1100 )
Result:
```

- vea (a2) memory content where a2 points to

```text
.. 22 33 44 55 66 .. ..
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no STOREM. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T use an immediate `<vea>`.
